name: Jam: everyone in the car gets to DJ
object: Jam, the Spotify Premium feature that lets a group start and co-host a shared, real-time listening session
audience: friend groups who fight over who controls the music on a drive or hangout
message: This video tells friend groups that with Spotify Premium, nobody has to fight over the aux cord — everyone in the car can add to the same live session together.

moments.what: A girl in the passenger seat turns to the driver and claims control of the music; in the next shot, several friends packed in the back seat all hold up their phones at once, each wanting to pick the song.
moments.copy: So guys, who's playing music? It's me.

moments.what: Close shot of the girl smiling smugly, then a hand holds up a phone showing the Spotify home screen with a Jam icon visible among the navigation options.

Hands tap through the app to start a Jam; a 'Join Tanya's Jam?' screen appears offering to continue on this phone or play from Tanya's speaker, then a shared queue fills with songs from different friends.
moments.copy: Spotify — I start and host a Jam with Spotify Premium.

moments.what: The whole car sings and laughs together, phones still in hand, everyone visibly part of the same shared playlist.
The car drives off down a tree-lined road as bold on-screen text reads the feature name, followed by the Spotify Premium logo and an upgrade line.
moments.copy: Start and host a Jam. Spotify Premium — upgrade now.

cta: On-screen text 'Start and host a Jam' over the car pulling away, followed by the Spotify Premium logo and an 'Upgrade Now' line.
why: Opening on a petty fight for music control is instantly recognisable to anyone who has shared a car with friends, so the UI steps that follow (search, join, shared queue) read as solving that specific friction rather than showing off a feature in a vacuum. Ending on the group singing together before the logo lands the message: Jam is sold as a group feeling, not a screen.
